title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 9
preview: Maddox is a spam filter, THE Dictator is second in points and 7-9, Brad's points against need their own zip code, Cardillo's perfect lineup is still last, and Mike's QB lasted one snap. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Week 8 gave us a 194-point Commish, a matchup of the century decided by 50, four Penix interceptions, a tenth defense, and a quarterback who lasted one snap. Week 9 kicks off Thursday, and the whole league is begging one man to beat Jacob. Nobody is safe.
facts_note: Every fact is real: Sleeper Week 8 results and lineups, season points for/against and max points, transactions through Wednesday Nov 4, Week 9 matchups, and the 2020-2025 ESPN archive for the all-time head-to-head. Streaks are head-to-head only. A roast among friends.

entries.roast: What is the deal with Maddox? He's 13-2-1, best record in the league, and I went through his transaction history to see the genius at work. Four real moves all season. Four! The rest is the Commish adding Shedeur Sanders to his roster and Maddox deleting him. Six times! Once in 12 minutes! That's not a GM, that's a spam filter. The man hasn't touched his roster since October 24. He's not building a dynasty, he's ignoring an inbox. And the whole league is in the chat begging "someone for the love of God beat Jacob." Beat him? You can't even get him to log in.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer: 13-2-1 against 7-9, first against seventh. The whole league has a rooting interest Sunday, and for once it's THE Dictator. Fuck you Maddox.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 12 without logging in.

entries.roast: Second in the league in points. Seven and nine. THE Dictator has outscored everybody but Maddox and still has a losing record, which takes a special kind of leadership. He's left 171.8 points on his own bench this year. Thirty-two waiver and free-agent moves, and that's what he built: a bench. One win snaps a four-game skid and he's "so fucking back." Back to what? Seventh? And the 194 came against Brad. Congratulations. You beat the guy everybody beats. Engrave that one yourself.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox: 7-9 and one week removed from a four-game skid, against the best record in the league. Ryan gets to be the people's champion for exactly one Sunday.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 12, and THE Dictator reviews the tape for collusion.

entries.roast: Water. Earth. Fire. Air. Long ago, the league lived in harmony. Then Maddox attacked. Only the Avatar, master of all four elements, could stop him. But when the world needed him most, he vanished. Lost by 50. Left Dalton Kincaid's 19.1 on the bench for Michael Mayer. Last week we said Brian couldn't lose if he tried. Turns out he just hadn't played anybody. Lowest points against in the league. Fifth in scoring, second in the standings. I used to think Brian was unbeatable. I still do, but I used to, too.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet: 11-5 with the streak snapped, against 10-6 coming off a win. Second against third, a game apart. Brian finds out what it's like to play someone who shows up two weeks in a row.
entries.prediction: Mike wins by 6, and Brian answers the chat Tuesday.

entries.roast: Brad has given up 1,426 points this season. That's the most in the league by almost 200. Every team he's played has dropped at least 144 on him. Six straight losses. You'd think a man getting mugged every Sunday would at least lock the door. Nope. Both his starting running backs went on IR before the weekend, Pierce on Wednesday, Harvey on Saturday, and Brad's Sunday-morning fix was Samaje Perine. 2.9 points. He'd have done better leaving the spot empty and saving the stamp. Brad isn't unlucky. Unlucky is losing a coin flip. Brad keeps calling heads on a coin that's already on the floor.
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman: six straight losses against four wins in five. Brad's season can still be saved, just not by anyone on his roster.
entries.prediction: Drew wins by 22, and Brad has money on Drew.

entries.roast: Rashee Rice. Tee Higgins. D'Andre Swift. Sam Darnold. Kyle's left 257 points on his bench this season, more than anybody in the league, and he still won three straight. Over Ryan, Drew and Taylor. Mate, that's not a gauntlet, that's a Tuesday. So naturally Kyle's calling himself a "Dark Horse." You're 9-7, Kyle. That's not a dark horse. That's a horse. A horse with 257 points sitting in the stable because the jockey can't read a projection.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo: 9-7 and three straight wins, against the defending champ at the exact moment the defending champ is the worst team in the league.
entries.prediction: Kyle wins by 18, and Gronk Nation goes 7-1 in the last 4.

entries.roast: Kasik announced that his team is "the definition of mid." That's generous. He's eighth in points. Sunday, Joe Burrow threw for 45.6, the best quarterback day in the league, and Kasik lost by 19. Zay Flowers gave him zero. Christian Watson, the receiver he traded his best receiver for, gave him 18.8, and it didn't matter. Highest score in the league once, lowest twice. That isn't mid. That's a client with a great alibi and a terrible lawyer.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado: 7-9 against 4-12 and dead last. Kasik is favored against last place, and somehow that's still the scariest sentence in his week.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 14 and files it under mid.

entries.roast: Drew started the season 0-3, with a 98.25 in Week 3, the lowest score in the league that week. Now he's 8-8, he's won four of five, and the new act is humility. He tells Brad he'd be "beyond shocked" to drop 140 on him. Drew. Could you drop 140 on Brad? I could see that happening. I could see that as a possibility. Yes, I suppose. Meanwhile Chase Brown, projected 18, sat on his bench for 16.1 while Ollie Gordon, projected 13, gave him 6.9. Drew benched his best running back and still won by 19. That's not modesty. That's a man who wins by accident and calls it character. Eight and eight. Perfectly balanced. Half the time he's lucky, and the other half he's Drew.
entries.this_week: vs Bradley Kochheiser: 8-8 and winning against the longest active losing streak in the league. Drew's only job Sunday is to not make it interesting.
entries.prediction: Drew wins by 22 and calls it lucky.

entries.roast: Mike has made 47 transactions this season, most in the league by a mile. Waivers, free agents, four trades. And here's what he built. Lamar came back from three weeks out and lasted one snap. Thumb surgery, IR. His backup, Baker Mayfield, went 0-for-3. Zero completions, all day. His kicker, Jason Myers, missed an extra point. The free one! DeVonta Smith is catching passes from Tanner McKee, when he's catching passes at all. Forty-seven moves and the roster looks like a pileup on I-96. Forty-seven! The man has traded for everything in this league except a quarterback who can finish a game. Mike, buddy, you ARE 911. And Tuesday night at 8:45, 911 called us: "Gents I desperately need qb … send me trades."
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill: 10-6 and one game back of second. Win Sunday and Mike can pull even for the second seed. He's never been this close to being a contender and this far from a quarterback.
entries.prediction: Mike wins by 6 with whatever quarterback he finds by Sunday.

entries.roast: Michael Penix Jr. had thrown one interception all season. One! Then Cardillo started him. Penix had never thrown four picks in a game. Then again, he'd never played for Cardillo. And here's the part that hurts: Cardillo's dead last in points, and even if he'd started his perfect lineup every week he'd have 1,128, the lowest ceiling in the league. He's not underachieving. This is the achievement. The defending champion didn't defend the title. He threw it to the other team four times.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano: 5-11 against three straight wins. The Belt is still in Boston for now, but the standings say not for long.
entries.prediction: Kyle wins by 18, and Penix throws one to Gronk Nation.

entries.roast: Week 1, Taylor dropped 232. He's spent seven weeks proving it was a clerical error. Lowest score in the league two weeks running. Wednesday he found the Bengals defense, his tenth defense of the season. Ten! Most men get through a whole marriage with fewer commitments. At this rate he'll have rostered all 32 before he wins another game, and honestly, it's closer than it sounds. The Bengals gave him 4.45, so this morning he cut them for the Lions. Eleven. He's not building a roster, he's speed dating. Then he started Omar Cooper Jr. at flex for zero, with Jonah Coleman's 21.9 and McConkey's 13.1 on the bench, both projected higher. Lost by 39. Somewhere a waiver claim is filing a missing-persons report.
entries.this_week: vs Nicholas Kasik: last place and three straight losses, against a team that just lost by 19 with the best QB of the week. Taylor finally has a matchup to feel good about.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 14, and Taylor adds defense number twelve by Friday.
